chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Aqeeqa of the boy and the girl is a ram.

key_terms.عَقِيقَةُ: Aqeeqa: the sacrifice offered on the occasion of a child's birth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for Aqeeqa sacrifice for boys and girls?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the baseline legal ruling for Aqeeqa, specifying that the sacrifice for both a male and female child is identical: a single ram (kabsh). While this narration confirms the equality of gender in the obligation, Shia jurists often contextualize this within broader discussions where some scholars recommend two rams for a male and one for a female based on other narrations, highlighting the distinction between obligatory minimums and recommended virtues (mustahabb).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘
Aqeeqa of the boy and the girl, is a ram’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Shu’ayb from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
‘Aqiqah for a boy or a girl is one ram.’”
